commands.reactionrole.add.description: Bind an emoji on a message to a role
commands.reactionrole.clear.description: Remove every binding of a message
commands.reactionrole.description: Let members pick roles by reacting
commands.reactionrole.list.description: List the bindings of a message or of the whole server
commands.reactionrole.param_channel: Where that message is (defaults to here)
commands.reactionrole.remove.description: Unbind one emoji from a message
modules.reaction_roles.description: Emoji ↔ role bindings: members get or lose a role by reacting. Bindings are stored, so they survive restarts.
modules.reaction_roles.name: Reaction roles
reaction_roles.add.done: {emoji} → {role} is now bound on [this message]({url}). Members get the role by reacting with that emoji.
reaction_roles.bad_emoji: `{value}` is not a usable emoji. Use a Unicode emoji (e.g. 😀) or a custom one as `<:name:ID>`.
reaction_roles.bad_message_id: `{value}` is not a valid message ID. Use the digits from "Copy Message Link".
reaction_roles.bot_missing_manage_roles: The bot lacks Manage Roles in this channel, so reactions would not actually grant anything. Grant it first.
reaction_roles.clear.done: Removed {count} binding(s) ([message]({url})). Roles already handed out are not taken back automatically.
reaction_roles.list.stale_role: ⚠️ the role is gone; this rule is cleaned up the next time somebody reacts
reaction_roles.list.title: Reaction role bindings
reaction_roles.notify.failed: I could not give you the role **{role}** in **{guild}** (most likely the bot's role sits lower than it). It has been logged — ask an admin to take a look.
reaction_roles.notify.granted: ✅ You now have the role **{role}** in **{guild}**. Remove your reaction to give it up.
reaction_roles.notify.removed: ➖ You no longer have the role **{role}** in **{guild}**. React again to take it back.
reaction_roles.remove.not_found: There is no {emoji} binding on that message.
